title: Concept Drills — Computational Methods or Mechanics (Class 11 Mathematics)
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Why do numerical methods (like Newton–Raphson) solve equations by REPEATED approximation instead of exact formulae?
questions.solution: Most equations (x = cos x, high-degree polynomials) have no closed-form solution — no formula exists. Iteration replaces the impossible exact answer with a REFINABLE estimate: each step reduces the error, and stopping after enough steps gives any desired accuracy. Approximation with control beats an unattainable exact form.

questions.question: Explain the geometric idea behind the Newton–Raphson iteration x_{n+1} = x_n − f(x_n)/f′(x_n).
questions.solution: At the current guess x_n, draw the TANGENT to the curve; where the tangent crosses the x-axis is the next guess — usually closer to the root. The formula is just the tangent's x-intercept. Each iteration follows the tangent downhill toward the root; near a simple root it converges quadratically (digits double each step).

questions.question: A picture hangs from two wires at angles. What conditions must the two tensions satisfy for equilibrium?
questions.solution: Two conditions: the horizontal components of the tensions cancel (ΣFx = 0) and their vertical components together equal the weight (ΣFy = 0). Two equations, two unknowns — solvable. Equilibrium means the vector sum of ALL forces is zero: no net push in any direction.

questions.question: Why is it easier to open a heavy door by pushing at the handle far from the hinges than near them?
questions.solution: The turning effect (moment) = force × PERPENDICULAR distance from the pivot. The handle maximises that distance, so the same force produces a much larger moment. Near the hinges the distance is small — most of your force is wasted. Distance from the pivot multiplies the force's effect.

questions.concept: Projectile motion as two independent problems
questions.question: Why can a projectile's horizontal and vertical motions be solved separately?
questions.solution: Gravity acts only vertically, and the horizontal velocity has no vertical component — the two axes don't interact. Horizontal: constant velocity (no horizontal force). Vertical: constant acceleration g. Solving each axis with its own simple equation, then recombining, gives the full trajectory — independence of perpendicular components is the principle.
